whatThisIs: GRAHA DHŪPA is the incense — and, adjacently, the gandha, the scent or scented paste — offered to the nine grahas in graha-śānti and navagraha-pūjā. IT IS NOT SAMIDHA and IT IS NOT NAKṢATRA-VANASPATI, and this dossier's central finding is that the sources themselves keep those columns apart. In the Yājñavalkya-family grahaśānti passage the dhūpa is ONE substance for all nine grahas — guggulu (L01-s1, L02-s1, L02-s2, L03-s1, L04-s1, L07-s1, L08-s1) — while the samidha, the homa fuel-woods, ARE enumerated graha by graha in the very next verses of the same passage (L01-s4, L03-s4, L06-s4, L08-s3). One verse apart, one differentiated and one not. The Matsya recension of the same rite names no incense substance at all, only 'fragrant' (L06-s1). So THERE IS NO PER-GRAHA INCENSE TABLE IN THE TIER A LAYER READ FOR THIS ROUND, and a site column that shows one is showing something the classical texts do not say. What the classical layer does differentiate about the fragrant offering is its COLOUR: Vijñāneśvara's Mitākṣarā glosses yathāvarṇam as the colour of the flowers and scents offered to that planet (L02-s3). Per-planet incense lists do circulate, and they are 21st-century commercial and astrologer's web copy that cites no text and disagrees cell by cell (L16 vs L17); they are recorded here at Tier C, labelled, with the disagreement preserved. Two further things are recorded as warnings and are NOT data: an 'aroma oils and planets' page that enumerates Neptune, Uranus and Pluto and is Western correspondence repackaged under graha names (L18-s3, L18-s4, L18-s5), and a 'Plants and Planets in Indian Astrology' page that merges European herbal magic with Ayurveda under one 'Vedic' heading (L19-s1, L19-s2) — which is precisely the conflation this round exists to avoid. This is a living tradition practised by millions; nothing here asserts that any of it works, and nothing here is addressed to a reader as instruction.
headlineFinding: The Tier A grahaśānti layer has ONE dhūpa cell, not nine. The per-planet incense grid that the site's Western column has an analogue for does not exist in the Sanskrit sources read this round; it exists only in modern commercial copy, which contradicts itself.

entries.forWhat: ALL NINE GRAHAS COLLECTIVELY (navagraha) — NOT a per-graha assignment. One substance for all nine.
entries.english: Guggulu — a resin. The 11th–12th c. Mitākṣarā identifies it no further than 'a kind of resin' (L02-s2, OCR 'a land of resin').
entries.botanical: Commiphora wightii (syn. C. mukul) — COMPILER-SUPPLIED standard modern identification. NO source in this ledger names a botanical species; the sources say only 'guggulu' and, in the commentary, 'a kind of resin'. The identification is offered as a lexical gloss, not as an attribution.

entries.variants: The Matsya Purāṇa recension of the same rite names NO substance, only 'fragrant' (surabhi) — see the Matsya row, which ships beside this one and is not merged with it. In the modern commercial layer, guggal is narrowed to Jupiter alone (L17-s5), i.e. one graha receives what the classical texts give to all nine.
entries.note: THE CENTRAL ROW OF THIS DOSSIER. The half-verse 'gandhāś ca balayaś caiva dhūpo deyaś ca gugguluḥ' — scents and bracelets, and guggulu is to be given as incense — stands in the grahaśānti passage of Yājñavalkyasmṛti 1.299 (L01-s1), Agni Purāṇa 164.5 (L03-s1), Nārada Purāṇa I.51.83 (L07-s1) and Garuḍa Purāṇa I.101.6 (L08-s1), with the PD English of Vidyarnava 1918 at L02-s1 and Vijñāneśvara's gloss at L02-s2 making the distributive reading explicit: all the planets are offered the same incense. THESE ARE NOT FOUR INDEPENDENT WITNESSES — the Garuḍa colophon itself calls the passage 'the grahaśānti spoken by Yājñavalkya' (L08-s2), so this is best described as one passage in four transmissions. CONTRAST, NOT CONTENT: in every one of those texts the samidha are enumerated graha by graha within a few verses of this one (Yj 1.302 at L01-s4; Agni 164.8 at L03-s4; Garuḍa I.101.9 at L08-s3; Matsya 93.27 at L06-s4). Those sids are named here so a reader can check the contrast; they are NOT cited as support for this row and no homa wood belongs in an incense column.

entries.variants: This is the recension conflict, and BOTH ship. Matsya P. 93.18 (L06-s1) occupies the same position in the same rite as the Yājñavalkya-family verse — garments and flowers by the graha's colour, then the dhūpa — but where they read gugguluḥ it reads surabhi. Neither reading is preferred here and neither is merged into the other. Later in the same chapter dhūpa reappears in an undifferentiated list of worship items (L06-s2).
entries.note: WHAT THIS CHAPTER DOES ITEMISE GRAHA BY GRAHA is the naivedya, the food offering (L06-s3), and the samidha (L06-s4) — neither of which is incense and neither of which is carried here. ONE TRAP FLAGGED BY THE FETCHER AND NOT WALKED INTO: Matsya 93.143 (L06-s5) names candana, aguru and kuṅkuma, but as substances anointing palāśa sticks in the chapter's vaśya/uccāṭana appendix, not as any graha's incense. It is the easiest verse in the chapter to misread as a per-planet incense assignment and it is not read as one here.

entries.forWhat: EACH GRAHA INDIVIDUALLY — but the differentiated variable is COLOUR, not substance. This is the only genuinely per-graha cell the Tier A layer has for a fragrant offering.
entries.english: Scents / scented paste, offered in the graha's own colour. The substance is not specified.
entries.botanical: None named. The texts specify a colour, not a plant.
entries.variants: The same colour-not-substance shape recurs in the Tier C astrologer's-handbook layer: BPHS ch. 84 directs the flowers and garments of the colour belonging to the planet, with sandal and guggul undifferentiated (L11-s2).
entries.note: Yj 1.298 (L01-s3, PD English at L02-s4), Agni P. 164.4 (L03-s3) and Nārada P. I.51.82 (L07-s2) direct that the grahas be drawn in their own colours, with scents on the maṇḍala, and that garments and flowers be given 'according to colour'; Garuḍa I.101.5a says the same (L08-s4). Vijñāneśvara glosses yathāvarṇam explicitly as the colour of the flowers AND SCENTS offered to that planet (L02-s3). SO A PER-PLANET COLUMN CAN HONESTLY CARRY A COLOUR HERE; IT CANNOT HONESTLY CARRY A SUBSTANCE. The individual colours per graha were not the object of this round's retrieval and are NOT recorded in this ledger — see the gaps entry on graha colours before any colour cell is filled.

entries.note: TIER C DELIBERATELY, on the fetcher's reasoning and this compiler's: the extant BPHS is a late and disputed compilation, and the text read is R. Santhanam's astrologer's-handbook translation (Ranjan Publications, 1984), in copyright, on an archive.org upload of doubtful legitimacy (see ledger L11 'pd'). NOTHING FROM IT MAY BE REPRODUCED ON THE SITE; it is verification-only fair quotation in the ledger. The row earns its place because the handbook layer independently agrees with the classical layer that the incense is undifferentiated. The same chapter DOES give per-graha samidha in Hindi plant-names (L11-s3) and per-graha image metals (L11-s4); neither is dhūpa, neither is carried here, and the image-metals line in particular ('red sandalwood' for one graha) is the kind of cell most likely to be mistaken for an incense assignment.

entries.note: TIER C: modern website copy from a widely used panchang/paddhati portal (Drik Panchang). Recorded because it is the live, mainstream, present-day form of the rite, and because it shows the undifferentiated dhūpa is not merely a textual archaism — it is what the ordinary contemporary vidhi still does. This dossier records the structure of the offering only; it carries no claim about what the rite achieves.

Fennel = Foeniculum vulgare. Musk is animal-derived, not botanical. COMPILER-SUPPLIED identifications throughout.

contestedPoints: HOW OLD IS THE TIER A LOCUS? Bühnemann states that the Yājñavalkyasmṛti's chapter on Vināyaka and the nine heavenly bodies, vv. 270ff., is not an original part of the work (L12-s1). Since Yj 1.299 is the anchor of this dossier's headline row, the row's date is contested at its root: the passage is early relative to everything else here, but it is not evidence for the antiquity of the Smṛti as a whole. Both positions ship; this dossier does not date the passage.

HOW MANY WITNESSES IS 'FOUR TEXTS'? The identical half-verse stands in Yājñavalkyasmṛti, Agni P., Nārada P. and Garuḍa P. — but the Garuḍa colophon itself calls the chapter 'the grahaśānti spoken by Yājñavalkya' (L08-s2). Read one way that is four independent attestations of a single practice; read another it is one passage in four transmissions and the convergence is philological, not evidential. THE SECOND READING IS THE CONSERVATIVE ONE AND IS THE ONE THIS DOSSIER USES; the first is recorded because the ledger does not settle it. Either way, frequency of attestation is evidence about transmission and never about efficacy.

GUGGULU vs SURABHI. Matsya P. 93.18 (L06-s1) stands in the same position in the same rite and names no substance where the Yājñavalkya family names guggulu (L01-s1). Both readings ship, attributed, unmerged. Choosing the tidier one would be the merged-conflict error this protocol exists to catch.

IS GUGGULU A GRAHA INCENSE AT ALL, OR JUST THE DEFAULT ŚĀNTI INCENSE? The Atharvavedapariśiṣṭas use guggulu, usually with kuṣṭha, as the standard śānti incense in rites that have nothing to do with planets (L10-s1, L10-s2, L10-s3), and Nārada P. uses guggulu alone as a general dhūpa well outside the graha chapter (L07-s3). On that reading the graha rite inherits the ordinary śānti incense rather than being assigned one, which would make even the single Tier A cell a weaker claim than it looks. Geslani's abstract supports the general proposition that astrological ritual adapts Atharvan śānti (L14-s1) — BUT ONLY THE ABSTRACT WAS READ (L14-s3) and he is not cited for this specific point. Recorded as an open question, not resolved.

THE TEXTS HAVE THE VOCABULARY AND DO NOT USE IT HERE. Nārada P. I.79.288–290 contrasts a many-substance dhūpa with guggulu alone (L07-s3); the Bṛhatsaṃhitā compounds named incenses in a dedicated chapter (L09-s2, L09-s3) and allots incense by class of being in the puṣyasnāna (L09-s6); the Īśānaśivagurudevapaddhati has a ten-ingredient daśāṅga (L13-s1). Differentiated incense is a thing these traditions can express. That they do not express it for the grahas strengthens the confirmed-absent finding — but it is an inference about intent and is labelled as one.

THE TWO MODERN LISTS DISAGREE CELL BY CELL. Sun: sandalwood (L17-s1) vs saffron and rose (L16-s1). Venus: kastūrī (L17-s6) vs sandalwood and camphor (L16-s6). Jupiter: guggal (L17-s5) vs saffron and kevaḍā (L16-s5). Mars: agar/oud (L17-s3) vs red sandalwood (L16-s3). Mercury: tulasī (L17-s4) vs cardamom and champa (L16-s4). Saturn: vetiver (L17-s7) vs musk, frankincense and fennel (L16-s8). They disagree even about HOW MANY CELLS THERE ARE: nine (L17-s8, L17-s9) vs eight, with the nodes merged (L16-s9). The one convergence is the Moon and jasmine (L16-s2, L17-s2). A practitioner source states the variance from inside the tradition (L20-s1, L20-s2). NEITHER LIST IS PREFERRED AND NEITHER IS MERGED.

ONE MODERN LIST CONTRADICTS ITSELF. Gemstone Universe assigns rose to the Sun (L16-s1), jasmine to the Moon (L16-s2) and champa to Mercury (L16-s4), then states that Venus is angered by champa, jasmine and rose (L16-s7). That is not a conflict between sources; it is a conflict inside one page, and it is the best available measure of how much weight the Tier C layer can carry.

ONE 'VEDIC' AROMA LIST IS NOT INDIAN AT ALL. Astroshastra's 'Aroma Oils and Planets' runs to twelve entries whose last three are Neptune, Uranus and Pluto (L18-s3, L18-s4), and its Ketu cell includes Palo Santo, a South American wood (L18-s5). It is Western aromatherapy and planetary-magic correspondence repackaged under graha names. IT IS RECORDED AS A PROVENANCE WARNING AND IS NOT AN ENTRY IN THIS DOSSIER. Nothing from it may reach any Vedic column.

THE CONFLATION EXEMPLAR, NAMED SO IT CAN BE RECOGNISED AGAIN. Astroshastra's 'Plants and Planets in Indian Astrology' merges European herbal-magic material — dragon's blood, belladonna, henbane and the rest — with Ayurvedic material under a single 'Vedic' heading (L19-s1, L19-s2), gives Rāhu an undivided list unlike the other grahas (L19-s3), and its only gesture at incense is an unidentified 'incense tree' (L19-s4). It is herbs and trees, not incense, so it is not dhūpa data; and it is not usable as vanaspati or samidha data either. IT IS RECORDED AS AN EXEMPLAR OF THE EXACT MERGE THIS ROUND EXISTS TO AVOID, AND IS NOT AN ENTRY. SAFETY: that page lists belladonna and henbane, both acutely toxic, with no flag of any kind on the source page (L19-s2).

EVEN THE SHOPPING LIST KEEPS THE COLUMNS APART. A commercial navagraha-pūjā samagrī list itemises nine colour-differentiated cloths and nine sacred threads beside a single undifferentiated line for incense sticks (L22-s1), and puts 'Havan Samidha Sticks' on its own separate line (L22-s2). The distinction this round was told to protect — homa wood is not incense — is one the modern trade still observes.
honestLimits:
WHAT THIS DOSSIER IS NOT. It is not a per-planet incense table, because the sources read do not contain one; the shape of the result IS the result. Twenty-two rows ship and seventeen of them are Tier C modern commercial copy recorded so that the label travels with the data — they are not a recommendation that the site render them.

SOURCES. No critical edition was consulted directly. The Sanskrit is GRETIL e-text, which carries its own 'for reference purposes only' notice, and the Yājñavalkya file rests on the 1949 Nirnayasagara edition; verses are cited, not that edition's apparatus. The public-domain English route (Vidyarnava, Allahabad 1918, PD by date) is raw archive.org OCR with visible corruption — 'mcense' for incense, 'a land of resin' for a kind of resin — and the OCR is quoted as found rather than silently repaired. Gangadharan's Agni Purāṇa, Santhanam's BPHS, Bühnemann 1988 and Prajith 2008 are all in copyright; they appear in the ledger as short verification quotations only and NONE of them may be reproduced on the site. The BPHS scan is additionally of doubtful legitimacy as an upload. Geslani's article was never obtained beyond its abstract and is cited for nothing else; his monograph was not obtainable at all.

WHAT WAS NOT READ, AND COULD OVERTURN THIS. The Viṣṇudharmottarapurāṇa graha chapters (GRETIL 404). The Śāradātilaka and Mantramahodadhi — the tantric paddhati layer, where deity-specific dhūpa is routine and where a per-graha list is most likely to exist if one does. The Bhaviṣyapurāṇa. The 1857 Navagraha Vidhāna Paddhati, which is public domain and whose OCR is simply unusable. Any of these could carry a per-graha dhūpa, and the headline finding is a finding about the texts that WERE read — it is not a finding about 'the tradition'.

COVERAGE. Nothing South Indian and āgamic; nothing regional; nothing in Tamil, Telugu, Kannada, Malayalam or Bengali; no manuscript material; no temple paddhati; no ethnography of what practitioners actually burn. A tradition practised by millions across many regional ritual grammars is represented here by six Sanskrit texts and six websites.

IDENTIFICATIONS. Botanical binomials, Devanagari forms and most Sanskrit equivalents in the Tier C rows are COMPILER-SUPPLIED lexical glosses, marked as such in the fields themselves; no source in this ledger identifies a species. Where a vernacular name is genuinely ambiguous — 'red sandalwood', 'champa', 'frankincense' — the ambiguity is left open rather than resolved, because resolving it would manufacture a precision the sources do not have, and in the case of red sandalwood the resolution would also determine whether a CITES-listed species is involved.

SAFETY AND PROTECTION FLAGS. Three protected or threatened species appear in one nine-cell commercial list — Aquilaria agarwood, musk-deer musk and Nardostachys jatamansi — and all three protection notes come from the FETCHER'S ANNOTATIONS (L17-s3, L17-s6, L17-s8), not from the product page, which carries no conservation notice at all. Every other conservation or toxicity flag in this file is compiler-supplied and explicitly marked UNVERIFIED IN THIS LEDGER; each must be checked against a real conservation source before any shipped page states it. Health effects of incense combustion were outside this round's retrieval entirely and no claim about them is made in either direction.

WHAT IS DELIBERATELY ABSENT. No quantity and no process parameter anywhere, per FRAMING §5 C-1 — the sources read give none for the dhūpa either, so nothing was withheld that they supply. No efficacy, medical or life-outcome claim: several Tier C sources make them and the fact that they do is recorded while the claims are not. No samidha and no nakṣatra-vanaspati has been allowed into any row; where a samidha sid is named it is named inside a note as a contrast and never as a supporting citation. No timing or day-of-week assignment, although two Tier C sources supply them. And no colour cell, although colour is the one thing the Tier A layer really does differentiate — because the per-graha colour list was not fetched this round and filling it from anywhere else would be the fabrication this protocol was written to stop.
